correctness.rationale: Each nonzero Fourier mode of the exact hydrodynamic linearization has generator A_k. The Hermitian part has maximum eigenvalue -k²-1+sqrt(1+(Pe kr/2)²), making strict singular norm growth equivalent to Pe²r²>4(k²+2). The first mode is sharp and the energy inequality controls all other modes globally. The independent eigenvalue formula yields the previously known modal threshold, and its exact difference is the square Q(3r-2)²/[r²(1-r)(2r-1)]. At r=2/3 every A_k is Hermitian. At half filling exact triangular exponentiation bounds the gain between Pe C_L and Pe C_L+1, with C_L>0 attained. Symbolic identities and selected matrix exponentials replayed with the included verify.py; finite numeric tests are not used to establish infinite-dimensional claims.

value.rationale: A sharp physically fixed species-density norm distinguishes short-time response from the already-known spinodal eigenvalue instability. The result locates spectrally stable but amplifying active-gas states with a complete analytic parameter window and a unique symmetry-induced collapse at density 2/3. At half filling it gives an unbounded, explicitly optimized activity-linear transient gain even though every modal decay rate is activity independent; this makes the distinction operationally consequential rather than an arbitrary numerical example. It motivates finite-noise susceptibility and near-spinodal transient tests without asserting that those downstream results have already been proved.
